newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks ride miners to steady end.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks ride miners to steady end.

text.p: The Australian share market closed barely changed on Friday after early Wall Street-induced selling in the banks petered out and support for the major miners emerged at the day's lows.
The All Ordinaries index lost a point to 2,475.3.

The big banks suffered most on the day from a spike in bond yields but bounced off the bottom as the initial bout of selling dissipated, while a modest rally from the resources sector, buoyed by a stronger gold price, led the afternoon rebound.
"It rallied in the afternoon," said broker Robert Cameron of Cameron Securities, pointing to the way the sell side dried up.
"It looked like a lack of sellers more than anything else."
The gold sector impressed with the gold index adding 1.6 percent after the bullion price jumped overnight.
Great Central Mines, up eight cents at A$3.28 (US$2.54), and Normandy Mining, up seven cents at A$1.75, were the pick of an almost universally firmer sector.
Qantas Airways flew high after Thursday's first half net profit of A$151.6 million. Its shares closed up eight cents at A$2.54 after touching a record high of A$2.57.
Melbourne casino operator Crown Ltd topped turnover lists with 14.27 million shares traded, the bulk of it in a number of lines specialled through Prudential Bache Securities.
Its scrip ended five cents lower at A$2.37.
Rises shaded falls just by a whisker, while about 28 percent of stock traded remained steady.
